subject: Encryption and KMS evidence request — Greenleaf SIG/CAIQ
messages:
From: Alex Tully <alex.tully@greenleafbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenleaf Bank Security <security@greenleafbank.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: encryption/KMS evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — we’re kicking off the SIG/CAIQ intake for a planned production pilot and have a handful of specific asks on encryption and key management before our security council signs off. Can you please provide or point us to the following artifacts?

- High-level diagram showing where customer data is encrypted (at-rest vs in-transit) and where customer keys are stored/managed (Redwood KMS vs customer BYOK/HSM).
- HSM attestation or summary of HSM-backed key protection for any BYOK flows.
- A sample of key rotation logs (audit-level, redacted) showing a rotation event and operator identity.
- KMS configuration/export (ideally a small YAML or JSON snippet showing key policies, TTLs, and replica regions).
- Confirmation of zeroization/crypto-erase procedures on account termination.
- TLS ciphers and minimum TLS version for external endpoints.

We can accept redacted logs and a short narrative for any proprietary details. Would it be possible to get this package by Friday so our CAIQ mapping team can progress? If not, can we schedule a 30-min intake call tomorrow?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Tully
Security Engineer, Greenleaf Bank
alex.tully@greenleafbank.com


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tully <alex.tully@greenleafbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: encryption/KMS evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. I can turn around a compact package and a short narrative. Looping in Ben (crypto/security lead) and Hannah (compliance) to confirm scope and any redaction rules.

Ben / Hannah — Greenleaf is asking for KMS/HSM evidence, rotation logs, and zeroization confirmation. Can we:

1) Prepare a 1-page diagram and a brief narrative covering at-rest vs in-transit controls.
2) Export a sanitized KMS config snippet (kms-config) and a CSV sample of a rotation event (redacted UIDs).
3) Attach our HSM attestation summary for BYOK flows and a short note on zeroization on contract termination.

Alex — are you okay with redacted operator IDs and truncated timestamps in the rotation sample? Also, does your team need the full CAIQ mapping or just the raw artifacts to map against questions?

If the Friday turnaround is tight, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow at 11am PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Tully <alex.tully@greenleafbank.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Nov 2028 13:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: encryption/KMS evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Alex / team — attaching the artifacts below. Notes on each:

Attachments:
- redwood-kms-config.yaml (attached) — contains the KMS key policy snippets, rotation cadence defaults, and cross-region replication flags. Sensitive fields are masked.
- hsm-attestation-summary.pdf (attached) — non-PII summary of our HSM provider attestation, FIPS levels, and whether key material is wrapped in HSM (BYOK paths).
- rotation-log-sample.csv (attached) — redacted sample showing a rotation transaction, operator role (redacted to role level), and KID fingerprint.
- transit-ciphers-and-tls.txt (attached) — list of accepted ciphers and minimum TLS version for externally-facing endpoints.

Quick answers inline:
- At-rest: customer data encrypted using tenant-specific data keys; keys are either Redwood-managed KMS keys or customer BYOK (wrapped in HSM). See diagram and kms-config for details.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred; we publish accepted ciphers in the attached file.
- Zeroization: on contract termination we perform key destruction for Redwood-managed keys and provide a certificate of destruction. For BYOK, we provide guidance and coordinate key escrow/return; we do not retain unencrypted customer key material.
- Rotation: rotations are automated for system keys on a set cadence; customer-controlled keys require an operator action. Audit trails include event id, timestamp, source host, operator role, and KID (we’ve redacted user identifiers in the sample).

If you need a signed HSM attestation (vendor-signed cert) instead of this summary, let us know and we’ll elevate.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

[Attachment stubs: redwood-kms-config.yaml (text), hsm-attestation-summary.pdf (pdf), rotation-log-sample.csv (csv), transit-ciphers-and-tls.txt (txt)]
From: Alex Tully <alex.tully@greenleafbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Nov 2028 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: encryption/KMS evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Marissa / Ben — this is perfect, thank you. The redactions are fine for initial mapping. A few follow-ups from our CAIQ team:

- Can you provide a sampled copy of the certificate-of-destruction template you issue to customers?
- For BYOK flows: confirm whether any Redwood logs ever contain unwrapped key material (explicit yes/no).
- Would you be able to provide a vendor-signed HSM attestation PDF within the next week? If so, we’ll flag that as high priority.

We’ll proceed with the mapping and may have a couple of CAIQ question numbers to route back to you. If it helps, we’ll also share the list of SIG/CAIQ control IDs we map to.

Thanks again — Alex
